facts.value: Industry categories are a way to organize and understand different types of industries. Industries can be categorized as heavy or light, domestic or foreign, durable or non-durable, or manufacturing or construction industries.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Biochemistry

facts.value: Heavy industries require a large initial investment and often employ a capital-intensive production process. Examples of heavy industries include the aviation sector, the automobile sector, and natural resource harvesting sectors like steel and coal. These industries typically have high capital requirements.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Biochemistry

facts.value: Light industries, on the other hand, have lower capital requirements and often rely on labor-intensive production processes. The restaurant sector is an example of a light industry.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Biochemistry

facts.value: These categories can help businesses and investors understand the characteristics of different industries and make informed decisions.
facts.programme_association: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Biochemistry
